runs.t: The CIA triad identifies three fundamental security properties: Confidentiality, Integrity and Availability. It helps teams translate vague security goals into explicit controls and measurable risks.

For confidentiality, restrict who can read sensitive data; for integrity, prevent or detect unauthorized modification; for availability, maintain service through faults and attacks. Threats often affect more than one property, so evaluate them together.
In a hotel PMS, guest contact details need access control and encryption; payment records need integrity checks and audit; bookings need backups and recovery to remain available.
Maximizing one attribute can harm another: strict checks may add latency, broad replication may enlarge exposure. Prioritize according to asset value, threats and regulatory needs.
